Pre-exceptional basic EPS: critic raised a concrete objection: The 1.31p anchor you used for FY2025 is almost certainly the half-year (H1 FY2025) pre-exceptional basic EPS from the interim results (shown as 1.31p vs 4.03p, -67%), not the full-year FY2025 figure. Using an H1 number to project a full-year FY2026 EPS is a period mismatch and will understate the base. Check the FY2025 full-year pre-exceptional basic EPS in the FY2025 annual results/RNS instead of the H1 1.31p.
Pre-exceptional operating profit: critic raised a concrete objection: You used £45.6m as the “prior-year FY2025” base, but £45.6m is H1 FY2025 pre-exceptional operating profit (vs £105.1m in H1 FY2024, -57%), not a full-year FY2025 figure. Building an FY2026 full-year forecast off a half-year base is the wrong fiscal period/basis and will understate the result.
Net fees: critic raised a concrete objection: The base you use is a unit/scale misread: “prior-year same period H1 2025 (-1400)” improperly treats a “(1.4)” in the H1 FY25 table (e.g., Australia & New Zealand 74.3 (1.4) …) as -1,400 GBPm of net fees. That “(1.4)” is a percentage change (−1.4%), not an amount, and Hays’ H1 FY25 Group net fees are positive and in the low hundreds of £m, not negative £1.4bn. With the base off by orders of magnitude and wrong sign, the derived FY2026 276.044 GBPm is invalid.

Averaging those non‑contiguous swings to proxy FY2026Q3 is a wrong basis and effectively just carries forward FY2025Q3 (~$580m) with no justification tied to the actual FY2025→FY2026 period.
